_comment: IGT is not a table. Snow Peak calls it the LAYOUT SYSTEM (レイアウトシステム), and the
frame is one node in it: frames join to each other and to a family of other tables.
Two constants hold that family together, and Snow Peak publishes neither -- they are
read off the dimensions, the same way the 250mm unit pitch was:
400mm  the fire-side datum. EVERY table in the system stands 400mm tall, and the
IGT Low leg (CK-112) is 400mm. So 'the Connection Table is compatible with
IGT using Low Height Legs' is not a suggestion, it is arithmetic.
496mm  the shared depth. The IGT frame is 496 deep; the Takibi My Table is 496 deep;
the corner pieces are 496 square. They meet flush.
Every rule below quotes the vendor copy it came from. Where no rule could be sourced,

LV-381.name: Connection Table
LV-381.evidence: "compatible with most IGT Extensions using Low Height Legs, and can be connected with the Jikaro Firering Table to create an extended fire-safe table space."

ST-050.name: Jikaro Firering Table
ST-050.evidence: "compatible with the Iron Grill Table for additional extension possibilities." Built to ring a Takibi Fire & Grill -- the 600mm opening is the fire pit. It stands at 400mm, the system datum, so anything hooked to it takes the 400mm IGT Low leg -- and Snow Peak's own photo (JP a011) shows exactly that: a Bamboo IGT Table hooked to one outer edge, standing on 400mm legs, its near end carried by the Jikaro.
_it_is_four_pieces: FOUR identical trapezoid segments, and they go together either way round. That is not
a detail -- it is two different tables, and the planner needs both.
The two plan views (JP a007 = long edge inward, a008 = short edge inward) are shot at
DIFFERENT SCALES, by a factor of 1.26, so nothing can be read across them directly.
What crosses is the SEGMENT: it is the same physical piece in both, so its long side,
short side and height are the invariant, and they are what ties the photographs
together.
a007, long edge in  : outer 1069px, opening 565px, straight sides 347px
a008, short edge in : outer 1068px, opening 439px, straight sides 712px
the scale ratio, read off the segment three ways:
long sides   712/565 = 1.260
short sides  439/347 = 1.265
heights    314.5/252 = 1.248        agree to 1.4%
Calibrate on the published 1120x1120 / opening 600 -- which is the a007 config, because
its ratio 0.53 matches and a008's 0.41 does not -- and everything falls out, and CHECKS:
segment: long 600, short 365, height 260mm
(slant ~24 deg. The outer chamfer comes out at 45 deg for free, whatever the sides
are -- it runs from one segment's outer corner to the next one's, and symmetry
does the rest.)
the SHORT side is measured TWICE, independently: 364mm as a007's outer straight edge,
366mm as a008's opening. And a008's bbox comes out 885 predicted vs 890 measured.
Two photographs at two scales agree with each other and with the spec table, once the
scales are kept apart. That is the check that says the model is right.

long_in.name: long edge in (spread)
long_in.note: The published configuration -- the spread/'long edge in' assembly the user calls WAI-BEN (outward). A 600mm fire opening (= a 2-Unit IGT bay when bridged), and four short 365mm outer edges to hook onto.

short_in.name: short edge in (compact)
short_in.note: Compact -- the 'short edge in' assembly the user calls NEI-BEN (inward), Snow Peak's 'square mode'. A 365mm opening (= a 1-Unit IGT bay when bridged) and four long 600mm outer edges. The same four pieces, turned around.

Like the connection hook and rail joint, a bridge cannot stand alone -- it modifies the Jikaro. See layout.bridges. Opening 600 -> 2-Unit bridge, opening 365 -> 1-Unit bridge; the opening size is what decides which fits.

_comment: The connection model, made explicit. FIVE interface mechanisms; the HOSTS that expose them
(ports); the GUESTS that attach via them; the ADAPTERS that convert one interface to another.
This is the authoritative taxonomy -- the app's legalOn / edgeKeysOf / hostEdge / slot machinery
currently encode the same rules by hand; migrating them to read THIS is the plan. Passed through
untouched by build_catalog (it only special-cases tables/joints/corners/ecosystems).
connections._model: A guest attaches to a host PORT when their interface matches (directly OR via an ADAPTER that bridges the port's interface to the guest's). SCALE (table | board) does NOT gate the connection -- it decides SUPPORT: a table-scale guest (a frame) MAY join a board-scale port (a rail joint's output, a board's bracket), but that port can't bear it, so the frame stands on its OWN legs there (a warning if the user drops a pair). All INFERRED from this -- no hard-coded pairings. Interface keys are unified; `label` is the human name.

ext_table.label: IGT Extension Table (ET)
ext_table.desc: the IGT frame hook interface -- an extension table / corner / another frame joins here.

side_rail.label: IGT Side Rail
side_rail.guest_side: brackets grip / a rail joint hangs
side_rail.desc: slide or hang along a continuous long rail.

slot.label: IGT Slot
slot.desc: a module drops INTO a unit, flush at the datum.

hanging.label: IGT Hanging Accessory
hanging.desc: a rack hooks OVER the rails and hangs below; still consumes units.

knob.label: Knob (ツマミ)
knob.desc: built-in aluminium knobs on the top's side lock two pieces DIRECTLY -- symmetric, no host/guest, no CK-175. The SAME joint the Jikaro's four segments use between themselves, so its outer edges ARE that port; 'the Jikaro as one whole' is our abstraction over four knob-joined segments. Only the heat-resistant fire-table system (Jikaro + Connection Table) has it.

hearth.label: Fire-ring aperture
hearth.host_side: the ring's central opening (600 spread / 365 compact)
hearth.guest_side: the pit's own footprint, standing on the ground
hearth.desc: The APERTURE of a fire ring, at ground level. Not a slot and not an edge -- nothing hooks, and nothing is BORNE: the ring merely stands around a pit that carries itself on its own feet, which is why a guest here takes no leg from its host. It is a port because the ring is BUILT around it: a Takibi Fire & Grill L is 455mm square, so it goes in the 600 and cannot go in the 365 -- the arithmetic decides, and no list has to be maintained. Owner: ringing the fire is the standard application (定番) -- 'if you move the table there is no reason not to move the fire pit' -- which is exactly a host-guest relation and NOT an ad-hoc multi-selection. The guest stays usable ALONE; hosting here is optional, like every other port.

ST-050.note: The fire ring's reason to exist. Gated by FIT, not by a list: only a pit that measures inside the opening is offered, which is the whole of 'the big ring takes the Takibi'. A Takibi Fire & Grill L is 455mm square -- into the spread form's 600, never the compact form's 365.
ST-050.correction: MINE, caught the same hour I wrote it. I first noted here that the compact 365 takes the GS-1000 by bridging the opening into a 1-Unit bay for GP-040 to drop into. That is false twice over and I wrote it without checking. GP-040 is span 3 = 1.5 UNITS = 375mm; a bridged compact opening is 1 Unit = 250mm, so GP-040 does not go there at all. The owner's two statements are two INDEPENDENT routes, not one chain: (a) the GS-1000 stands in the compact ring's opening DIRECTLY -- it is round and the JP spec is written as a diameter, so if phi-350 is right it clears 365 by 7.5mm a side, exactly as the Takibi L clears 600; (b) the GS-1000 ALSO mounts in an ordinary IGT bay via GP-040, the 1.5U joint frame -- which needs a real 2u/3u/4u frame and is already modelled as a slot_module. Route (b) has nothing to do with this port.
ST-050.resolved_dims: SETTLED from the GS-1000 manual's own spec table (data/manuals/GS-1000.pdf p1, 仕様): 外形寸法 使用時 phi-350 x h420mm, 収納時 phi-240 x H205mm, 重量 1,800g. So phi-350 IS the diameter and 420 IS the height -- and 350 < 365 confirms the owner: the compact ring's opening is cut for this stove, exactly as the spread's 600 is cut for a 455 Takibi. My earlier doubt ('420 does not sit with an 800g stove') was right that a number was misread, but wrong about WHICH: the stove is 1,800g, and the catalog's 800g was a PARSER bug (the thousands comma -- see scripts/fetch_jp_specs.py WEIGHT_RE). The manual was a scan with no text layer; rendering the page and reading it settled in one pass what prose had left ambiguous for weeks.
ST-050.unresolved: GS-1000 is STILL not wired into this port, for a different reason now: it has no MODEL. Its role is `accessory`, so kindOf sends it to `table` and it would draw as a tabletop; it needs a prop kind and a builder (tripod legs with length-adjust buttons, wind screen, rotating gotoku, the canister slung under on a hose -- all of it drawn in the manual's 各部の名称 diagram, which is a good source). Only then does `guests["GS-1000"] = {via: "hearth"}` earn its place. The measurement blocker is gone; the geometry one is not.

corner.note: a corner's far bracket is a BOARD-scale ET port -- the run turns 90 deg through the corner and the NEXT board chains on here (same as any board's bracket)

XCK-128.desc: clips into the long rail so an ET board or a hanging accessory can attach where there is only a rail. The ET port it creates is BOARD-scale -- a joint holds a board, not a frame.

CK-175.desc: gives a frame end a hook so two table-scale ET ports (two frames, or a frame and a Jikaro) can join -- the frame system's stand-in for the knob.

tta.name: Table Top Architect
tta.note: A SEPARATE system, not an IGT accessory. TTA clamps to the edge of ANY tabletop — an IGT frame, a bamboo extension, a Takibi table, someone else's table — and hangs its own fittings off it. It coexists with IGT constantly, which is why it is easy to mistake for part of it, but nothing in it depends on the IGT grid: a TTA clamp consumes no unit and cares only that there is an edge to grip.

CK-151.name: IGT Height Adjuster

CK-151.evidence: "allow for integration of different table heights. Set your cooking space to a standing height, then dining while seated. To use, slide into the edge of the IGT Frame, then attach the next table at preferred height and tighten the knobs."

CK-175.evidence: JP catalog: IGTコネクションフック.

parts.attach_evidence: ATTACH: the copy never says how the angle extensions attach, and their plan view shows the hooks only if you look for them on the SLANTED edge -- which the detector could not, because it tested for protrusion past the BOUNDING BOX. Two sources settle it. LV-381's manual, in English: 'it is possible to connect this product with a Bamboo IGT Table Regular / Long, Bamboo Left/Right Angle Extension, Bamboo Left / Right Corner Extension (CK-117TR, CK-218, CK-219, CK-118TR, CK-119TR)'. And the owner pointed at the hooks in the top view and at the close-up (JP a009): the same stainless wire hook, let into a slot in the board's edge, arching out and bending straight down. DEPTH: Snow Peak publishes 990x496, but that aspect (1.996) contradicts its own photograph (2.13) by 7% -- on BOTH mirror products, from two independent shots, while CK-117TR and CK-119TR agree with theirs to 0.6% and 0.3%. The hook spacing settles which number is wrong: it must match the frame's end holes (287.8mm), and it is 288-292mm on every other bamboo board. At the published scale CK-218's hooks come out 304mm apart -- a 5% outlier that would not enter the holes. At 990x465 they come out 289mm, the scale is isotropic (1.3866 vs 1.3881 mm/px), and the published WIDTH is reproduced to 0.4%. So 990 is real and 496 is not the bounding box; what Snow Peak means by it, I do not know, and am not going to invent. This matters because the ANGLE is measured in this frame: at the published scale the leg reads 61.2deg (turn 57.6), and at the true one 59.7deg (TURN 60.0).

parts.material: アルミニウム合金、ステンレス
parts.curated_reason: IGTコネクションフック -- what joins two frames END TO END. A frame's end already has the HOLES (measured on CK-149: x = +/-406.5, z = +/-143.9); CK-175 supplies the other half by turning the neighbouring end into a HOOK. It is JP-only, has no manual, and exactly ONE real photograph in its gallery -- which happens to be of exactly this: two frames butted end to end, black end pieces face to face, two knurled thumbscrews spanning the joint, and TWO PAIRS OF LEGS bunched at it (so the frames do not share legs; each keeps its own four). The JP spec table says セット内容 本体×2 and 45g(本体一つあたり) -- a pair, 45g EACH -- so one set makes one joint (one hook per hole) and the SET weighs 90g. The scraper took the 45 as the item weight, which is what the page literally says and is not what it means.

Packed 500x110x360 reads the same way: 500 wide, 110 THICK, 360 deep -- the body with its cover clamped on. parts.material: ステンレス
parts.curated_reason: 焚火台グリルブリッジL: two flat stainless rails on four folding notched straps that hook over the Takibi L's rim, carrying the cooking surface. NOT a placeable node -- and that is not our call, it is a safety instruction in its own manual, under 警告: 「本製品は焚火台Lにセットした場合にのみ安定する構造です。単品で自立させてものを置くと転倒事故の原因になります」. A part that tips over if you set it down has no position. Same standing as ST-051/CPL-JT2U on the Jikaro: a toggle on its host, billed, never its own node. 445x440x175 / 収納 ...x28 / 1.6kg published.

parts.title_en: Fireplace Coal Bed L (Charcoal Bed Pro. L)
parts.title_jp: 炭床ProL
parts.material: 鋳鉄（クリア塗装）
parts.curated_reason: 炭床Pro.L: a 310x310x20 cast-iron GRATE (a slotted slab with a raised logo boss and four little feet), 3.9kg -- published. It has no legs and no position of its own: it WEDGES into the bowl's taper wherever the square section is 310, which at bowl_depth 200 is 64mm below the rim -- and the JP a001 shows it exactly there. That is its whole purpose (raise the burn floor, burn less charcoal). A toggle on the Takibi, billed, never a node.

parts.curated_reason: 焼アミPro.L, 484x352x19 -- the full-size net, and a part that ties this branch to the IGT bill: Snow Peak's own compatibility copy names ST-032GBR / ST-032R / CK-160 in one breath. 484 is deliberately BIGGER than the Takibi's own 455 rim: it is sized to land ON the bridge's rails, not to drop inside the bowl.
